transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-02-15 08:00 PT / 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 58 minutes (recording): Zoom
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Alex (MapleHome Procurement), Priya (InfoSec), Daniel (Legal), Sam (Platform), Lina (Finance)

Summary:
Short gateway call for procurement/technical gating. Customer wants to confirm MSA/DPA redline surface, KMS expectations, SLA guarantees for a pilot, and any egress/data residency pricing flags before putting to procurement committee. Also scoped required artifacts: SOC2 summary, private deployment diagrams, and a pilot SLO sheet.

Topics covered:
- MSA / DPA redline items and typical enterprise exceptions
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs and costs
- KMS/HSM integration, key rotation, and RBAC
- SLA matrix, SLOs for pilot, and rollback/fallback policies
- Pricing approvals, egress fees and billing cadence
- Next steps for legal/procurement review cycle

Action items (called out in conversation): see action_items metadata

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (AE): hey everyone thanks for hopping on, uh quick intro we're Maya and Jordan from Redwood Inference, we'll walk through the procurement and security checklist and then cover a brief tech layout for the VPC options.
[00:18] Alex (Procurement): thanks, appreciate the agenda. We're trying to move to vendor committee next month — need the legal stuff in by end of feb. Key ask: will you accept our standard MSA redline around indemnities and data handling?
[00:33] Daniel (Legal): yes specifically we need clarity on data processing flow, whether customer data is cached, and where audit logs live. Also curious re: DPA attachment and subprocessor list.
[00:47] Jordan (SE): ok, quick clarification — on hosted API we do prefix caching and KV cache is ephemeral on our side; for customers that need no caching we can toggle or use Private deployment where cache is fully under customer control. I'll share a short doc that shows default behaviors.
[01:10] Priya (InfoSec): from an infosec perspective KMS is the sticking point. We need customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) or HSM-backed key wrapping. Does Redwood support Cloud KMS integration or HSM modules for Private?
[01:28] Jordan (SE): yes, Redwood Private supports customer KMS integration (Cloud KMS, dedicated HSM) and we have integration patterns for envelope encryption + key rotation. There are two flows: 1) Bring-your-own-key (we never hold plaintext keys) or 2) Redwood manages keys but customer can request key rotation logs. For hosted we usually offer managed KMS with strict access controls but we can surface proof points.
[01:52] Alex (Procurement): that's helpful. Lina — any finance questions?
[01:57] Lina (Finance): main thing is pricing predictability. If we go hosted, we need clear egress and per-token pricing. If we pursue Dedicated, we'll commit to monthly reserved capacity—need the licensing terms and breakage/cancelation clauses spelled out.
[02:16] Maya (AE): we can provide a cost model sheet: hosted per-token rates, embedding rates, and a Dedicated reserved capacity proposal with commit tiers. We'll annotate cancellation windows and pro-rated refunds.
[02:29] Sam (Platform): technical Q: network topology — can we VPC peer with Redwood Private or do you require firewall tunnels? We have strict inbound policies.
[02:40] Jordan (SE): for Private we support VPC peering, transit gateways, and IP allow lists. For on-prem deployments we can do site-to-site VPN. I'll attach example diagrams. Note: peering sometimes requires route updates on customer side.
[03:05] Daniel (Legal): back to MSA — indemnity caps and data breach notification timelines. We require 72 hours notice of incidents, and we need an SLA credit mechanism. How do you typically structure SLOs and credits?
[03:25] Maya (AE): our standard is 48 hour-ish initial acknowledgement via support and 72 hour incident classification for major incidents; SLA credits are tiered — we can share a proposed SLA matrix with p99/p95 latency goals and availability thresholds. For enterprise deals we can negotiate specific credit formulas.
[03:47] Priya (InfoSec): do you have SOC 2 and ISO attestations? And do you offer penetration test reports or can we run a third-party pentest?
[03:56] Maya (AE): yes SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 summary we can provide, plus we have a pentest intake process. For Private/on-prem customers we allow scheduled assessments with scoping and NDA.
[04:12] Alex (Procurement): on subprocessors how granular is the list — do you list cloud infra vendors and CDNs? We need that for our DPA.
[04:21] Jordan (SE): we maintain a subprocessor list; we'll provide current snapshot with the DPA pack. For hosted there are more subprocessors (cloud provider, monitoring, storage), Private has fewer.
[04:34] Daniel (Legal): curious about data residency — can we restrict data to US only for the pilot?
[04:40] Jordan (SE): yes, we have region pinning for model serving. For the pilot we can route to US-only region and include that in the DPA. Note: some models might only be available in certain regions but we'll call that out.
[04:58] Priya (InfoSec): key rotation proof — do you provide rotation logs and KMS access audit events in an exportable format? We need those for compliance.
[05:08] Jordan (SE): yes exports and audit logs exist; if you run Private the logs are under your control. For hosted we can provide audit log exports for a retention window — let's align on the retention period you need.
[05:22] Alex (Procurement): timeline check — if we get the security pack + MSA redlines by next thursday, we can get to procurement committee by Mar 1. Is that feasible?
[05:33] Maya (AE): feasible. We'll aim to get the pack to you by Feb 18.
[05:38] Sam (Platform): quick technical probe — performance. We're running latency-sensitive search assistants; what are your p95/p99 numbers on the smaller LLMs and do you offer dedicated pools?
[05:52] Jordan (SE): yes dedicated GPU pools with reserved capacity are the path for consistent p99 spikes. Typical p95 for mid-sized models is in the low-100s ms for small seq lengths, p99 depends on batching and concurrency; we'll include a benchmark spreadsheet from similar customers.
[06:10] Lina (Finance): about pricing approvals — we may need a capex vs opex justification for Dedicated. Can you provide a one-page ROI showing unit cost before/after Dedicated?
[06:21] Maya (AE): yes, we'll produce a short cost-savings model comparing hosted vs dedicated for expected token volumes.
[06:29] Daniel (Legal): payment terms — are Net30 standard, and do you accept PO referencing the MSA? Also escrow?
[06:36] Maya (AE): Net30 is default; POs are fine. For enterprise we support escrow on certain negotiated items — we'll flag that for legal.
[06:45] Priya (InfoSec): two more security points: SSO/SAML SSO integration and RBAC. We need SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning and fine-grained RBAC to control who in MapleHome can call certain models.
[06:58] Jordan (SE): supported — SAML + SCIM provisioning is supported and RBAC fine-grained roles exist in the Console. We can share screenshots and mapping examples.
[07:12] Alex (Procurement): ok, can you confirm any non-standard redlines Redwood typically won't accept? helps speed legal.
[07:20] Daniel (Legal): yes specifically: full indemnity without cap, data escrow demands that the vendor host customer data on request without clear exit plan, or unlimited liability. Those are red flags.
[07:33] Maya (AE): understood — we'll call out hard stops in our MSA guidance doc. But, for Enterprise we can discuss tailored caps and carve-outs.
[07:44] Jordan (SE): small note on operations: for Private we can provide a runbook and onboarding plan, includes playbooks for upgrade rollback and patching windows. That usually satisfies platform teams.
[07:57] Sam (Platform): good — we need that runbook before pilot kickoff.
[08:01] Maya (AE): we'll include runbook + pilot SLOs in the pack.
[08:10] Alex (Procurement): final question — any early termination or migration support fees for moving off Redwood?
[08:18] Maya (AE): we include a migration assistance clause in enterprise deals and a standard export of logs + model artifacts; fees are negotiable. We'll document the migration path.
[08:29] Daniel (Legal): ok thanks; once we get the redline baseline we'll mark showstoppers and then schedule a short follow-up with legal only.
[08:38] Maya (AE): perfect — recap: Maya will send MSA/DPA + security pack; Jordan sends infra diagrams and SLA matrix; Priya will send KMS questions; Alex to schedule procurement committee. Any other items?
[08:53] Lina (Finance): none from finance.
[08:56] Priya (InfoSec): no, thanks.
[08:59] Maya (AE): thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts.

Call end.
